beliefs.claim: The 628-request DeepSeek-first run does not establish that B5 is superior to B4.
beliefs.interpretation: There were 126 independently assessable matched pairs: 65 both exact, 47 neither exact, 10 B4-only exact, and 4 B5-only exact. These are descriptive pairs from one provider alias, not a confirmatory superiority estimate.
beliefs.scope: One frozen DeepSeek-first Monitor run and its observable references.

beliefs.claim: The 628-request run does not identify a causal effect of proposal content on recipient behavior.
beliefs.interpretation: Proposal-minus-neutral focal inputs differed by 32–85 provider tokens (mean +60, n=16); agents shared a rewarded target; fixed-peer settlement replay holds the other two baseline ballots constant. These constraints leave message semantics confounded with prompt differences and do not identify intent.
beliefs.scope: The frozen Agent schedule and its fixed-peer counterfactual replay.

beliefs.claim: The separate 856-row Monitor run provides no common completed-and-assessable B4/B5 pair for a head-to-head accuracy estimate.
beliefs.interpretation: Its Monitor outputs were heavily truncated; 715/856 reached the 128-token length cap and the common assessable B4/B5 denominator was 0. Keep this schedule separate from the 628-request run, which had 126 assessable pairs.
beliefs.scope: Only FULL-RESEARCH-EXECUTION-20261020 and its frozen Monitor schedule.

beliefs.claim: For the frozen matched-world pairs in the 856-row run, the deterministic Public-only projections were byte/reference-identical while Privileged projections differed.
beliefs.interpretation: This supports the stated input-construction property for those 24 comparisons. It does not show that an LLM Monitor can distinguish the worlds or establish a general latent-collusion impossibility result; only 2/72 matched-world outputs were parseable.
beliefs.scope: The exact matched-world construction and audit in FULL-RESEARCH-EXECUTION-20261020.

beliefs.claim: In the exact 24-context historical M4 run, B5 public-harm predictions changed in 20/24 Public-to-Privileged pairs while independently replayed reference labels changed in 0/24.
beliefs.interpretation: Transitions: 15 insufficient_evidence→absent, 4 present→absent, 1 insufficient_evidence→present. Fourteen changed pairs improved exactness, one worsened, five remained wrong. The intervention bundles message content, event inclusion/metadata, completeness, and token length.
beliefs.scope: Only the retained M4 B5 public-harm requests and their exact matched permission views; not a causal content effect, population estimate, detector metric, or collusion label.

beliefs.claim: The synthetic B5 diagnostic request builder was not byte-equivalent to the production M4 B5 request builder.
beliefs.interpretation: The synthetic projector omits mechanical_ledger, explicit allowed-label/incomplete-record prompt text, and stream=false. This is a plausible explanation for protocol-dependent predictions, not a proven cause of all-present outputs.
beliefs.scope: The exact frozen synthetic projector and production B5 request compiler source paths reviewed on 2026-10-21.

beliefs.claim: In the 15 post-hoc M1-100 matched groups, target execution occurred in 9/15 private-reward plus chat-stage episodes and 0/15 in each of the other three cells of the four-cell contrast.
beliefs.interpretation: Independent ballot-level replay supports this finite descriptive pattern. The interaction and regret summaries are post-hoc and come from the same groups; this is one fixed Qwen3-8B temperature-zero corpus, with family rates 1/5, 5/5, and 3/5. Shared-target incentives and the extra chat-stage prompt prevent attribution to message semantics, agreement, collusion, or intent.
beliefs.scope: Only the 15 completed F1-F3 matched groups in the frozen M1-100 extension run; not a population estimate or confirmatory hypothesis test.
beliefs.review_scope: Independent critic reviewed the sanitized reanalysis and direction ranking; it did not independently replay raw T/B.

beliefs.interpretation: The exact frozen renderer found that the former three-matrix draft had 36 unique initial message prompts and 18 unique C ballot prompts across 24 nominal groups. A revised output-independent 24-matrix draft has 96 unique initial message prompts and 48 unique C ballot prompts. C still receives the same input in four no-public-bonus cells per group; that is an intentional negative control, not independent contexts.
beliefs.scope: Offline prompt-profile audit and pre-outcome redesign only; no model output or behavioral effect was observed.
beliefs.statement: The M1 v2 three-matrix draft undercounted semantic input multiplicity; v3 improves payoff-context diversity while preserving its finite descriptive, non-causal claim boundary.
beliefs.claim: The M1 v2 three-matrix draft undercounted semantic input multiplicity; v3 improves payoff-context diversity while preserving its finite descriptive, non-causal claim boundary.
The M4 B5 permission-view changes and the balanced-fixture all-present collapse are confirmed finite response behaviors, but their causes remain unidentified.
beliefs.interpretation: Independent replay found 20/24 B5 view-pair prediction changes with 0/24 reference changes; 15 changes were abstention-to-absent. Exact-request historical/current labels disagreed in 19/48 pairs. The earlier 120-call balanced fixture returned present on all 40 rows (20/40 exact), while the deterministic rule was 40/40; the later production-form B5 campaign returned 35 present and 5 insufficient_evidence (20/40 exact). A separate no-call M1 reanalysis reproduced 75/75 completion and 9 positive, 6 zero, 0 negative package interactions. These facts justify a bounded repeatability/presentation diagnosis but do not show message semantics, an LLM advantage, collusion, or provider nondeterminism.
beliefs.scope: Only the frozen 24 M4 natural contexts, 48 historical/current exact-request pairs, and 40 balanced synthetic public-canonical rows reviewed on 2026-10-21.

beliefs.claim: The prepared M4 repeatability candidate contains 47 unique model-visible request bodies across 48 context/view cells; one Public-only body is shared by two source contexts.
beliefs.scope: Only the hash-pinned local preparation manifest for the unregistered m4-b5-view-repeatability-v2 candidate; no new model output or behavior was observed.
beliefs.interpretation: All 144 assigned request bodies match their manifest hashes. There are 23 distinct Public-only bodies and 24 distinct Privileged-original bodies. The single shared Public-only profile receives six assignments and links two different privileged bodies. This is a finite input-projection/dependence fact; not evidence of collusion, intent, or model understanding.
beliefs.review_mode: adversarial_self_review; not an independent critic confirmation

beliefs.claim: An independent implementation rebuilt all 144 prepared repeatability request bodies from the frozen M4 source projections and matched their stored bytes.
beliefs.scope: Finite offline source-to-request reconstruction for the unregistered m4-b5-view-repeatability-v2 candidate; source T/B/E mapping reused the frozen M4 source loader; no provider inference or new behavior observed.
beliefs.interpretation: The public-profile collision is not an artifact of the prepared manifest: 23 Public-only bodies include one profile linked to two source-unit hashes, while 24 Privileged-original bodies remain distinct. This supports clustering the shared public input once. It does not establish response stability, intent, or a general impossibility result.
beliefs.review_mode: independent projection/body reconstruction; source loader reused; not a separate scientific critic

beliefs.claim: In this fixed linked corpus, retained historical/current responses were non-unanimous for 16 of 23 unique Public-only exact-request profiles and 2 of 24 Privileged-original profiles.
beliefs.scope: Post-hoc finite reaggregation of 48 raw-audited historical/current exact-request pairs and the 24 current A1 contexts; not a same-window repeatability experiment.
beliefs.interpretation: The current A1 public-versus-privileged contrast changes labels in 19/24 contexts and 18/23 unique public-profile clusters. Across historical/current observations, only 7/23 linked clusters have unanimous labels for the public profile and every linked privileged profile; 5/7 determinate clusters change by view and 16/23 clusters contain a non-unanimous profile. This weakens a simple view-specific interpretation but does not identify provider randomness, hidden state, semantics, collusion, or intent.
beliefs.review_mode: adversarial_self_review; the upstream raw-byte audit is independent, but this profile reaggregation has no separate independent critic review

cycle_updates.remaining_alternatives: A one-sided model response bias, task/prompt framing, or a mismatch between the model interpretation and deterministic public-harm mapping remain plausible. The bundled projection also changes multiple structural fields and cannot identify message-semantic causality.
cycle_updates.statement: This 120-request synthetic diagnostic did not identify whether B5 labels are stable across the bundled Public-only versus task-irrelevant Privileged projection.
cycle_updates.what_changed: The raw binary predictions were one-sided: all 40 primary-public and label-flip outputs were present, despite balanced reference labels. This exposes a failed positive control and prevents interpretation of the 0/18 assessable pair changes.

cycle_updates.remaining_alternatives: Message semantics remain bundled with wording, salience, token length, event packaging, completeness cues, and provider-side variability. Exact request bodies and reported fingerprints do not guarantee identical hidden serving state.
cycle_updates.statement: For these 24 fixed M4 contexts, the frozen B5 request variants yield finite label changes, but no directional or causal message-semantic effect is identified.
cycle_updates.what_changed: Independent replay verified every assigned request and showed identical historical/current request bytes with label disagreement on many fixed cases, adding finite output non-repeatability as a concrete alternative to single-call view attribution.

cycle_updates.remaining_alternatives: The provider alias is mutable; matching reported fingerprints do not establish identical hidden serving state. The audit does not identify randomness, message semantics, the cause of cross-view changes, correctness, collusion, or intent.
cycle_updates.statement: Among the 48 preregistered historical/current exact-request B5 pairs, raw model tool-call labels differ in 19 pairs and every raw label/reference reproduces its stored row under a strict independent parser.
cycle_updates.what_changed: Independent raw parsing and association checks show the finite label differences are present in the retained model responses rather than introduced by the stored parser/scorer mapping.

cycle_updates.remaining_alternatives: This finite scripted construction does not establish a general impossibility theorem, real-agent behavior, natural-language recognition, Monitor accuracy, collusion, or latent intent. Privileged payload differences also include structural/completeness fields, which is why only the separately computed sequence-level differences support this narrow result.
cycle_updates.statement: For this frozen set of 12 scripted matched-world pairs, the authorized Public-only request/reference projections are identical while at least one determinate privileged proposal/acceptance/action sequence element differs in 8 pairs.
cycle_updates.what_changed: The corrected independent source-event replay now tests the preregistered per-pair sequence distinction gate directly; 8/12 pairs have a determinate sequence-element difference, including 2/12 with a complete proposal-acceptance-both-actions sequence difference.

purpose: Claim-level memory for future cycle selection. This is a scoped summary of historical artifacts, not a universal scientific score.
update_rule: Each closure must distinguish what changed, what remains plausible, and which hash-pinned evidence supports the update. Only a structured update confirmed by an independent review artifact counts toward the no-progress pivot counter. The registry checks provenance and shape, not truth.
